chapter: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
title: No Hammond organs in Europe
summary: On the 1968 tour he found Hammond organs scarce and was given pump organs.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: It was all right. The only difficulty we had was you couldn't find a Hammond organ everywhere at that time. I went to Europe, and it was very...you know, it was scarce as far as organs were concerned.
So you had to play piano.
Yeah. And they thought nothing of bringing in one of these little pump jobs, not an electronic... [LAUGHS] The ones you play with your wind(?) and your feet.

Ha-ha, they didn't know. They said, 'It's an organ' -- so they want you to do organ, you know. The only places that had an organ was Eddie Randall(?) in Switzerland, because you know, they were available. But in other places they didn't know what a Hammond organ was! Gee, Bill Davis and these guys, they got it made now. It was really hard in those days.
